svg.aria-label: The software factory from goal to release
svg.text: THE SOFTWARE FACTORY: ONE GOAL IN, TESTED CODE AND A RELEASE OUT
AMAZON BEDROCK AGENTCORE RUNTIME · ONE microVM PER WORK ITEM
every call carries runtimeSessionId = sdlc-<uuid>, so every stage lands in the same microVM
stage: start that agent as a background task · status: new progress · read: one file · bundle: the workspace as a zip
/tmp/factory/<work item> one workspace, read and written by every stage in turn
GUARDS THAT KEEP A STAGE FROM HANGING
A stage never runs a command that does not return. It starts a test server in the background with a timeout.
A stage that sends nothing for 10 minutes fails with a reason. No stage runs longer than 80 minutes.
An MCP server whose command the runtime does not have is skipped, so it cannot fail every stage.
Every tool call is logged and streamed, so a quiet stage still shows what it is running.
THE RUNTIME SIGNS EACH OF THESE CALLS WITH SigV4, AS ITS EXECUTION ROLE
cli.py sends its own spans and your decisions too
AGENTIC SDLC AUDIT TRAIL · OPENTELEMETRY · ON BY DEFAULT
Metrics go to CloudWatch through its OTLP endpoint, and you query them in Query Studio. Spans factory.run,
call.<stage> and stage.<stage> go to X-Ray. Each stage start, tool call, and stage end is a line in the runtime log group.
Every call is signed with SigV4. Nothing issues a token, and no identity provider takes part.
